transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-07-09 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 46m
- Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Marisol Gomez (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (NovusAI Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (NovusAI ML Engineer), Jesse Mu (NovusAI SRE)

[00:00] Ethan: Thanks everyone for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes. Quick roll call — Marisol from infra and I'm the AE. Priya, do you want to quick intro?
[00:10] Priya: Yeah hi, thanks. I'm Priya, lead platform at NovusAI. We're building a multi-tenant inference gateway for internal teams and evaluating options for hosted vs dedicated deployments. Liam and Jesse are on to dig into integration/ops details.
[00:22] Liam: Hey, quick context — we're using a central gateway that routes requests to different backends. We want a drop-in Redwood adapter if possible, and compatibility with LangChain and LlamaIndex since several teams rely on those.
[00:34] Marisol: Awesome. Today we'll cover SDKs, connectors, proxying patterns, limits/quotas, and observability hooks. We'll also surface when Dedicated/Private is recommended.

[02:15] Ethan: To start — our SDKs are published for Python, Node, and Go. The quickstart repo is small, basically a single client instantiation and then call.generate or chat.stream. We also have a thin HTTP gateway example for teams that want to front Redwood with their own proxy.
[02:40] Liam: Do you have a LangChain example? Most of our notebooks import langchain.llm wrappers.
[02:47] Marisol: Yes — we maintain official LangChain adapters (and community LlamaIndex bindings). There's a cookbook gist and a small demo notebook. We'll share the notebook link. The adapter basically maps the LLM interface to Redwood's chat/generate endpoints and supports streaming tokens.

[05:05] Priya: Our gateway currently does auth, rate-limits per-tenant, and route-level routing. We want to avoid double-throttling. How does Redwood expose rate-limit/quota info so our gateway can make informed decisions?
[05:23] Marisol: Good question. For Hosted, we surface X-Rate-Limit headers on responses and a usage API you can poll. For Dedicated/Private you can configure quota policies at the customer route level and get webhook alerts when thresholds are hit. We also have a token-bucket style enforcement at the edge.
[05:45] Jesse: Do you support 429 retry headers or suggested backoff? Our gateway implements exponential backoff and jitter.
[05:52] Marisol: We return standard 429 with Retry-After where appropriate. For spikes we also proactively return a 503 with a body suggesting fallback model variants if you've configured them — that's the graceful-degradation route.

[08:04] Liam: On the SDK side — does the python client expose streaming in an async generator so our LangChain chains can stream directly?
[08:12] Marisol: Yes. Python async generator for streaming tokens; Node has an EventEmitter style stream. There have been a few minor cursor issues in older SDK versions — you might see token re-ordering in some edge cases; we've fixed most in 2025.05. We mark breaking changes in the release notes.

[10:27] Priya: For LlamaIndex specifically, we use the node-based connector for ingestion and retrieval. Do you support KV cache or prefix caching to reduce costs for repeated prompts?
[10:40] Marisol: Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching at the serving layer. For Dedicated you can tune eviction policies and cache windowing; Hosted has sensible defaults and cold-start protection. That said, caching works best when prompts are normalized — if you mutate tokens dynamically the cache hit drops.

[12:01] Liam: We're curious about embedding workflows — we use LlamaIndex to build indexes and call embeddings. Does Redwood have an embeddings endpoint and is that rate-limited separately?
[12:13] Ethan: Yes, embeddings is a separate endpoint and has its own quota buckets. We can expose per-route/per-key quotas so you can allocate a quota for indexers vs runtime queries.

[14:20] Jesse: Observability — we need tracing (OpenTelemetry), per-request IDs, and metrics (latency, tokens/response). What's available out-of-the-box?
[14:31] Marisol: We emit request-level metrics you can export to Prometheus via push gateway, and we support OpenTelemetry traces attached to requests (trace-id header propagation). The Console shows per-route latency percentiles and token cost breakdown. For Private we ship a local metrics scraper.
[14:58] Jesse: Good. How are logs handled for PII concerns? We need the option to disable transcript retention.
[15:05] Marisol: You can toggle retention and configure redaction rules. For Private deployments you control storage entirely. Hosted has configurable retention windows and a redact-on-ingest option.

[17:22] Priya: Integration pattern — the gateway will mediate authentication (SAML/OIDC) and sign requests to Redwood. Do you support internal JWT exchange or mTLS from gateways?
[17:33] Marisol: We support token-based auth, mTLS for Dedicated/Private connections, and SSO integrations for the Console. For per-tenant routing we'd suggest issuing short-lived tokens per-tenant via your gateway and passing them through.

[19:45] Liam: About model fallbacks — we have latency-sensitive routes and cheaper-cost routes. Can the gateway route to different model variants in Redwood automatically?
[19:55] Ethan: Yes, with Smart Routing policies you can define policy rules based on latency SLOs or cost. If a high-capacity model is saturated, the runtime can fallback to a quantized variant. We can expose those policy decisions via webhooks so your gateway can surface which model served the request.

[22:20] Jesse: On the proxy side — is there documentation for a sidecar pattern vs central gateway? We want to explore both.
[22:30] Marisol: We have two reference patterns: 1) sidecar per-service that calls Redwood directly, and 2) central gateway that proxies and enforces org-level policies. The sidecar reduces cross-service hop but complicates client SDK distribution. Central gateway simplifies quotas. We'll share both diagrams.

[24:40] Priya: Security check — SOC2 and encryption keys. Do you integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments?
[24:50] Marisol: Yes — Private and Dedicated support KMS integrations for envelope encryption and Customer-Managed Keys. Hosted supports bring-your-own-key options for certain enterprise tiers. We'll add our SOC 2 and ISO documents to the shared drive.

[27:18] Liam: A bit more on rate limits — when you return headers what fields are there? Remaining tokens? Remaining requests?
[27:27] Marisol: Headers include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, and for tokenized plans we also include X-Token-Budget-Remaining. The usage API offers historical usage to smooth gateway decisions.

[29:02] Jesse: How do you handle bursty traffic? Our gateways sometimes see bunched bursts from cron jobs.
[29:10] Marisol: We have burst buffers in the edge and configurable burst windowing on Dedicated. If the burst exceeds the buffer we surface informative 429s (or 503s if fallback is configured). For consistent cron spikes we recommend scheduling jitted retries or a background batch runner against the embeddings endpoint.

[31:40] Priya: About SDK versioning — we have multiple teams pinned to older langchain libs. Is it risky to depend on the SDK for compatibility or should we just call the HTTP endpoint from our existing wrappers?
[31:52] Ethan: Both are valid. SDKs give helper primitives (streaming, retries, typed responses). If you have stable wrappers we can provide a minimal HTTP example and a shim for LangChain so it's low-effort. Many customers do a small shim layer: wrapper translate -> call Redwood HTTP.

[34:05] Liam: LlamaIndex ingestion speed — can we batch embedding calls efficiently?
[34:13] Marisol: Yes, embeddings support batch endpoints. For Dedicated you can increase parallelism and we'd give guidance to aim for batch sizes that hit GPU amortization sweet spots. We'll include benchmark numbers from similar workloads.

[36:40] Jesse: Observability hooks again — can we inject our trace IDs into the token-level logs so we can correlate with application traces?
[36:48] Marisol: You can pass trace-id header. For Hosted we log trace-id in the request logs (subject to retention). For Private you can map traces to your tracing backend directly.

[38:55] Priya: Pricing— quick ballpark for Dedicated? We're sizing for initial 4 GPUs and autoscale to 8 for spikes.
[39:06] Ethan: I'll send a ballpark in email; depends on GPU type and commitment. For 4-reserved with moderate burst it's usually a mid-six figure ARR, but we can do monthly pilots. We'll include a detailed sheet in the follow-up.

[41:20] Liam: One thing — we've built a gateway proxy that rewrites prompts to insert prompt-engineering templates. Any concerns with that approach and Redwood's caching?
[41:32] Marisol: If you rewrite prompts heavily it'll reduce cache hits. If you canonicalize the variable parts and keep template fixed you get much better hits. Also consider using the KV cache for responses that are deterministic.

[43:10] Priya: Great — let's recap and next steps.
[43:17] Ethan: Recap: we'll share SDK quickstart repo and LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter snippets, Marisol will prepare a demo notebook and the reference gateway diagrams, we'll exchange PRD and security contacts, and schedule a 60-min SE scoping POC next week.
[43:32] Priya: Yep agreed. Jesse will send the gateway diagram and we'll look at Dedicated pricing.

[44:05] Marisol: I'll also include code snippets for token propagation (trace-id) and a sample webhook config for quota alerts.
[44:12] Ethan: Perfect. I'll follow up with the links: SDK repo, LangChain gist, dedicated pricing ballpark, and SOC2 docs.
[44:25] Priya: Thanks, everyone.
[44:30] Liam: Thanks, bye.
